title: Evaluation Contracts and Alerting Playbook for Model Certification
author: Kira Mendoza
body:
Overview
========

Purpose: This playbook defines the concept of an "evaluation contract" for models promoted into Redwood Inference serving fleets, and prescribes the alerting, monitoring, and triage behavior required to enforce those contracts in production. The goal is to reduce time-to-detect regressions, provide clear handoffs between applied ML and SRE/Platform teams, and make quantization/onboarding decisions auditable.

Scope: Applies to all models and model variants (float, int8, q4/q8) that are candidates for: Hosted API, Dedicated pools, or Private deployments. It covers pre-promotion acceptance tests, continuous observability, alert thresholds, and post-incident regression triage.

Definitions
-----------
- Evaluation contract: A machine- and human-readable specification (JSON/YAML) that describes the metrics, thresholds, datasets, and test harness configuration required for a model to be certified for serving.
- Certification owner: The applied-ml engineer or small team responsible for maintaining the contract and responding to alerts.
- Runtime monitor: Service (Datadog/Looker/Prometheus) checks that compare live outputs against the contract.

Principles
----------
- Contracts are versioned and immutable for a given promotion package (artifact id).
- Alerts should be actionable and include quick links to repro (eval-harness) and recent prompt examples.
- Minimal baseline: every contract includes latency, token-distribution drift, and at least two quality metrics (one automated, one human-reviewable).
- Acceptance gates are enforced automatically by CI and the deployment pipeline; soft alerts allow gradual rollouts when appropriate.

Contract Schema (summary)
-------------------------
A typical contract includes the following fields (example rendered here as human-friendly table):

| Field | Description | Example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| artifact_id | Model build id / git sha / registry tag | model-llama2-13b:v2.1 |
| suite_id | Reference prompt set id used for automated checks | sales-assistant-v1 |
| metrics | List of metric keys to monitor (AUC, BLEU, ROUGE, perplexity, toxic-score) | ["exact_match","helpfulness_score","toxicity"] |
| thresholds | Per-metric thresholds (warning/critical) | {"helpfulness_score": "warn:0.78;crit:0.65"} |
| latency_p50_p95 | Expected latency SLOs for the target deployment | "p50:40ms;p95:120ms" |
| quantization_profiles | Allowed quantization variants and acceptance tests | "q4f16:smoke, int8:full-eval" |
| owner | Certification owner (email/alias) | "ml-cert@redwood.com" |
| rollout_policy | canary percent / stage durations / fallback | "canary:5%:48h -> 25%:24h" |
| monitoring_queries | Links or snippets for runtime monitors | "/monitors/model-resp-time" |

Note: the above table is a human summary; the canonical contract is stored in YAML under the model's registry entry and referenced by artifact_id.

Pre-promotion checklist (automated + manual)
---------------------------------------------
1. Unit tests: small deterministic suites (tokenization, special tokens, serialization).
2. Automated eval: run eval-harness with suite_id across the following workloads: retrieval-augmented generation, multi-turn chat, instruction-following, and regression prompts. Record: metric breakdown, seed, hardware used.
3. Quantization smoke: for each supported quantization_profile run a reduced 300-sample pass and verify functional parity (exact-match delta), and KV-cache correctness.
4. Latency profiling: p50/p95/p99 on representative request size distribution. Artifact must meet latency thresholds defined in the contract.
5. Safety scan: run toxicity classifiers and a subset of adversarial prompt suite. Flag any sample exceeding toxicity thresholds.
6. Human review: product-facing example review (5–10 examples) from the certification owner and a cross-functional reviewer (SRE or product).
7. Sign-off: owner posts a release note with the contract reference and signs the registry entry.

CI/CD Enforcement
-----------------
- The model registry CI job executes the contract verification step. If any critical threshold is violated, the job fails and prevents promotion. Warnings are emitted to the rollout log but do not block.
- The deployment pipeline attaches the artifact_id and contract YAML to rollout metadata.

Runtime Monitoring and Alerting
-------------------------------
Required monitors (examples):
- Quality delta monitor: weekly aggregated difference between current model and baseline on production prompt-sample pool. Trigger: warn at 2 std dev drop, critical at 3 std dev.
- Latency SLO monitors: p95 > contract.p95 * 1.25 => warn; p95 > contract.p95 * 1.5 => critical.
- Token-distribution drift: KL divergence of token frequency over a rolling 24h window. Trigger: warn at 0.12, critical at 0.25.
- Safety spike detector: rate of responses flagged by online safety models. Trigger: warn at 0.5% of requests flagged, critical at 1.5%.

Each monitor must include: owner alias, runbook link, example failing queries (if available), and the artifact_id in the alert payload. Datadog monitor naming convention: redwood.model.contract.<artifact_id>.<metric>.\\

Alert routing and SLAs
----------------------
- Critical alerts page to PagerDuty: Certification owner and oncall-sre. Response SLA: acknowledge within 15 minutes, initial triage within 60 minutes.
- Warning alerts to Slack #ml-cert-notify and email digest. Owner to respond within 8 working hours.
- If the owner cannot remediate in-window, escalation to platform-eng lead is automatic.

Canary and Rollout Behavior
---------------------------
- Canary percentage and durations are read from contract.rollout_policy. Example: canary 5% for 48h with rollback on any critical alert; extend canary if warning alerts are present and owner approves.
- Automatic fallback: platform provides the ability to route requests to a pinned fallback artifact_id when critical alert triggers. The fallback should be another certified artifact with the same API compatibility.

Regression Triage Flow (high level)
----------------------------------
1. Alert fired -> PagerDuty page.
2. Owner acknowledges and posts a triage thread including: alert id, artifact_id, recent examples, and last good artifact_id.
3. Run quick reproducibility job: eval-harness --artifact artifact_id --suite sample-replay --limit 200.
4. If regression reproduces in eval-harness: tag as model-regression. Create a regression issue with priority P1/P2 depending on impact and attach artifact diffs.
5. If not reproducible: label as potential data-shift or runtime flake. Launch data-drift investigation (see Data Drift Appendix).
6. Remediation paths: rollback, patch (hotfix model), or reweighting (routing policy change).

Data Drift Appendix (short)
--------------------------
- Collect: sample of requests and responses (scrubbed), prompt metadata, client app version, and model artifact_id.
- Compare: prompt feature distributions (length, token types), response toxicity distribution, and average token counts.
- Trigger: if input distribution shift > threshold (JS divergence > 0.2) for > 12h, tag for product review.

Quantization Acceptance Tests
----------------------------
Minimum required tests per quantization_profile:
- Functional parity: 2k sample pass, metric delta <= contract.thresholds.functional_delta (default 1.5%).
- KV-cache integrity: 500 multi-turn replay samples checking state consistency.
- Inference stability: 100 deterministic seeds to detect non-deterministic tokenization regressions.
- Performance: p95 latency and throughput measured on target hardware (GPUs/TPUs) meeting contract latency profile.

Operational Playbook: example commands
-------------------------------------
- Run a diagnostic eval: eval-harness run --artifact model-llama2-13b:v2.1 --suite sales-assistant-v1 --limit 500 --record-output /tmp/eval.json
- Trigger a smoke quant test: quant-eval --artifact model-llama2-13b:v2.1 --profile q4f16 --samples 300
- Promote a certified artifact: model-registry promote --artifact model-llama2-13b:v2.1 --contract /contracts/model-llama2-13b-v2.1.yaml

Ownership and RACI (short)
--------------------------
- Applied-ML (owner): author contracts, run cert tests, respond to alerts, propose rollouts.
- Eng SRE/Platform: implement monitors, provide rollback tooling, own PagerDuty escalation.
- Product / CS: triage customer-impacting regressions and prioritize remediation.

Record-keeping and Audits
-------------------------
- Every certified promotion must include the contract YAML, test artifacts, seeds, and perf profiles stored in the model registry entry.
- Quarterly audits by Reliability and Applied ML teams will sample certifications and ensure contracts were followed and incidents were handled per SLA.

Maintenance
-----------
- Prompt sets (suite_id) must be reviewed every 90 days for relevance and updated with new user traffic samples.
- Contract thresholds should be re-calibrated annually or after major model family upgrades.
